title: Recursion remote execution backend manifest v1
description: Documentation/editor schema for scripts/remote/<name>.json. The authoritative, self-contained validation lives in scripts/remote_backend.py (no jsonschema dependency at runtime); this schema documents the contract and supports editor/CI tooling. A remote backend describes a service that executes work somewhere other than this box, pays from its own capacity pool, and returns a candidate that Recursion must independently verify. It is inert until a human sets RECURSION_REMOTE_ADAPTERS=1, RECURSION_REMOTE_<NAME>_ENABLED=1, the referenced env values, and RECURSION_REMOTE_LIVE=1. See docs/plans/remote-execution-adapters.md, docs/plans/recursion-v2-execution-fabric.md (Phase 6, Phase 7), and scripts/remote/README.md.

name.description: Must equal the manifest filename stem. Uppercased with dashes replaced by underscores, it forms the per-backend enablement flag RECURSION_REMOTE_<NAME>_ENABLED.

kind.description: cursor-cloud = an isolated vendor VM (scripts/cursor-cloud-adapter.py). grok-routine = a supervisory arm on an account-shared cloud computer, reached by an outbound signed routine webhook (scripts/grok-bot-dispatcher.py).

endpoint.description: Public https base URL, no userinfo, no query, no fragment. Exactly one of endpoint / endpoint_ref must be non-null. Use this form when the URL is not itself a secret (a vendor's public API base).

endpoint_ref.description: Reference to an env var holding the URL. Use this form when the URL is itself bearer-grade -- a signed routine webhook URL grants anyone holding it the ability to post to the routine. Durable records store this reference; the resolved value is never written down.

credential_ref.description: Reference to the env var holding this backend's own credential. Never a value. A reference naming a controller or deploy credential (GITHUB_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, or any name starting RECURSION_, SSH_, GIT_SSH, AWS_, HERMES_) is refused: a remote backend may hold exactly one credential, its own.

signing_key_ref.description: Required and non-null for kind grok-routine (an unsigned outbound routine call is not authenticated), and must be null for every other kind. Must differ from credential_ref.

capacity_pool.description: The account/subscription/quota that pays for work on this backend. Also the key of the concurrency lease: slots are held per pool, not per task.

host_id.description: The host class the work runs on, e.g. cursor-cloud (vendor isolated VM) or grok-bot-account-cloud (account-shared -- separate Bots are not separate security boundaries).

billing_basis.description: metered additionally requires RECURSION_ALLOW_METERED=1, the same rule the hermes engine follows. Usage records derive spend_state from this field and never from a vendor payload, so an unreconciled metered run cannot report itself as included.

on_demand.description: Permission to exceed the included quota. Setting it true also requires RECURSION_ALLOW_METERED=1. No error handler can set this: quota exhaustion is a defer (exit 75), never an argument for spending.

max_attempts.description: Attempts permitted per idempotency key (backend + operation + assignment_digest + dispatch_id + request_digest).

concurrency_lease.description: Simultaneous runs permitted against this capacity pool. Grok Bot ships with 1: every Bot on the account shares one computer, so two Bots editing code are one writer with two screens.

default_branch.description: Never a write target. Lucas merges here.

integration_branch.description: A disposable review artifact advanced only by the coordinator, after serialized ancestry, diff, scope and gate checks. Must differ from default_branch.

task_branch_pattern.description: Must contain the literal <task-id>. Substituted with the assignment's task_id to derive the isolated target branch.

allowed_result_branch_patterns.description: fnmatch patterns a returned branch must match. An unrestricted wildcard is refused: an external worker must not be able to return any ref. The default and integration branches are rejected before patterns are consulted, so a permissive pattern cannot readmit them.
